event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Kenvue’s 2024 Form 10-K situates COVID-19 within a broader category of ‘global health crises, epidemics and pandemics.’  Four years after the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic, management still describes the virus as a material, forward-looking hazard.  The discussion moves beyond boiler-plate language: it cites concrete transmission channels—commodity scarcities, shipping delays, supply-chain disruptions, labour-model changes (remote work) and demand volatility—while also recalling actual, mixed financial effects experienced during 2020-22 (gains in Self Care and Essential Health, fluctuations in Skin Health & Beauty).  Because the filing date (1 March 2024) is roughly four years post-event, the Time Decay principle calls for mid-range severity scores (≈4-6) when statements are event-specific and operationally detailed; more generic statements merit lower scores (≈2-3).  No snippet contains new quantified damage, and some mitigation efforts are referenced, tempering the ultimate risk ratings.  Overall, the pandemic remains an active, but now better-understood and partially managed, enterprise-wide risk for Kenvue.

evidence_list.snippet: A global health crisis, epidemic or pandemic may cause demand, supply and other operational challenges, which could adversely affect certain aspects of our business, results of operations or financial condition.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemics to broad business harm (‘demand, supply and other operational challenges … adversely affect’).
Forward-looking but generic—no specific functions or magnitudes cited.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic statement of pandemic-related adversity earns a modest mid-single-digit score consistent with a medium-term event.

evidence_list.snippet: We are subject to risks associated with global health crises, epidemics and pandemics, such as the global outbreak of COVID-19 and its variants.

components.reason: Names the specific event (‘COVID-19’) and frames it as a continuing risk exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct reference to COVID-19 raises relevance, but lack of operational detail keeps the score moderate.

evidence_list.snippet: Global health crises, epidemics and pandemics could adversely affect certain aspects of our business, results of operations or financial condition, including by causing commodity scarcities and other disruptions to our manufacturing operations, shipping delays and other disruptions to our supply chain and volatility in the demand for and availability and usage of our products.

components.reason: Enumerates concrete operational pain points (commodity scarcity, manufacturing disruption, shipping delays, demand volatility).
Covers both supply-chain and market-demand channels, indicating breadth of exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific operational mechanisms elevate this to the top of the mid-range (5) under the 4-year time-decay rubric.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, during the COVID-19 pandemic, although sales of some of our products, particularly in our Self Care and Essential Health segments, increased, sales of other products, particularly in our Skin Health and Beauty segment, fluctuated due to lockdown-driven lost usage occasions, including as a result of the inability of consumers to purchase our products due to financial hardship, government actions imposing travel or movement restrictions, shifts in demand and consumption away from more discretionary or higher-priced products to lower-priced products and consumer pantry-loading activity.

components.reason: Provides concrete, historical impact differentiated by segments, demonstrating real rather than hypothetical effects.
Details demand-side drivers (lockdowns, consumer hardship, mix shift) showing depth of risk analysis.
Mentions offsetting sales increases in other segments, partially mitigating overall severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Historical, segment-level effects show materiality but mixed outcomes; net score sits solidly at 4.
